selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main observation is made about the elements that make up created things?
questions.answer: They are described as spread across the entire earth.

questions.question: How are the species of created things presented in relation to the earth?
questions.answer: Each kind is shown as widespread over the earth in a unified way, almost as if it has taken possession of it.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the worldwide spread of the elements and species?
questions.answer: They must belong to and be produced by one single Creator.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat this conclusion as obvious and not merely probable?
questions.answer: Because the same materials and organized kinds are found across the earth in a broad, consistent way, which points strongly to one source.

questions.question: How are the elements compared to servants?
questions.answer: They are portrayed as mighty forces placed under command and made obedient.

questions.question: How are the species compared to soldiers?
questions.answer: They are pictured as orderly troops spread across the earth under one authority.

questions.question: What do these two comparisons together suggest about the Creator’s power?
questions.answer: They suggest complete authority over both the basic materials of creation and the many living kinds formed from them.

questions.question: What quality of the Creator is highlighted besides uniqueness?
questions.answer: Great power is especially emphasized.

questions.question: What does the passage say about giving a full proof of this point here?
questions.answer: It says the matter has already been explained elsewhere, so only a short indication is given here.

questions.question: After reflecting on these truths, what inner state does the traveler experience?
questions.answer: He feels an overflow of faith and delight in Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: According to the passage, what covers the whole earth: isolated individuals only, or the elements and species of creation?
questions.answer: The elements and the species of creation are the things said to cover the whole earth.

questions.question: What sign do the species carry wherever they spread?
questions.answer: They carry a mark that points to Divine unity.

questions.question: What does their worldwide spread imply about ownership?
questions.answer: It implies that they all belong to one Being.

questions.question: What does their worldwide spread imply about production or origin?
questions.answer: It implies that they all come from one Maker.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the relation between the elements and the One who uses them?
questions.answer: The elements are under His command like disciplined servants.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the relation between the species and the same One?
questions.answer: The species are under His command like organized soldiers.

questions.question: What is the effect of using images of servants and soldiers in this argument?
questions.answer: It makes the point that all these things operate under one will, one rule, and one power.

questions.question: What can be inferred about disorder or rivalry among creators from this description?
questions.answer: The passage leaves no room for rival makers, because everything is shown as serving one authority.

questions.question: Why is the statement about this truth kept brief in this passage?
questions.answer: Because the fuller explanation has already been given in other places.

questions.question: What combination of understanding and emotion marks the traveler at the close of the selection?
questions.answer: He has witnessed the Five Truths and feels both strong faith and happiness in Divine unity.

questions.question: In this passage, what is said about the basic materials of creation and their range?
questions.answer: They are said to extend over the entire earth.

questions.question: How does the passage move from observation to belief?
questions.answer: It points from the widespread presence of shared elements and organized species to the certainty of one Creator behind them.

questions.question: What two groups are included in the statement that they are the product and property of one being?
questions.answer: The elements with all they contain and the species with all their individual members.

questions.question: Why is including the individual members of species important to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows that not just general categories but even the many separate instances belong to the same single source.
